findings.title: SQL injection in admin login query
findings.detail: req.body.email is interpolated raw into models.sequelize.query SELECT (loginAdmin/Bender/Jim challenges). Untrusted input concatenated into raw SQL. Confirmed by reading source: `SELECT * FROM Users WHERE email = '${req.body.email || ''}' ...`.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: raw template-literal interpolation of req.body.email into sequelize.query; repro payload `' OR 1=1--`
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized query / sequelize replacements binding.

findings.title: SQL injection in product search query
findings.detail: req.query.q (criteria) interpolated raw into Products SELECT (unionSqlInjection/dbSchema challenges). `... name LIKE '%${criteria}%' OR description LIKE '%${criteria}%' ...`.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: raw interpolation of search criteria into sequelize.query; UNION-based injection reachable.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize the LIKE clauses.

findings.title: NoSQL injection via Mongo selector from req.body.id
findings.detail: req.body.id used directly as a Mongo selector {_id: req.body.id} with {multi:true} (noSqlReviews/forgedReview challenges). An attacker can pass a query object (e.g. {$ne:-1}) to update all reviews. Tool-missed by semgrep; recovered by LLM source review of the Mongo data flow.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: selector object built from untrusted req.body.id with multi:true; payload {"$ne":"x"} updates all docs.
findings.recommendation: Coerce req.body.id to a string / validate ObjectId; never pass raw user object as selector.

findings.title: Open redirect: substring allowlist check
findings.detail: isRedirectAllowed uses `url.includes(allowedUrl)` substring match (redirectChallenge), bypassable by appending an allowlisted URL as a query param. Confirmed at lib/insecurity.ts:138.
findings.recommendation: Parse URL and compare host against an exact allowlist.

findings.title: XXE via libxml.parseXml noent:true
findings.detail: libxml.parseXml called with noent:true on user-uploaded XML inside vm.runInContext (xxeFileDisclosure challenge), enabling external entity expansion / file disclosure.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: noent:true on attacker XML; classic XXE file-read payload.
findings.recommendation: Disable entity expansion (noent:false) / use a hardened parser.

findings.title: Server-side RCE via untrusted code eval (safeEval)
findings.detail: body.orderLinesData passed to safeEval (notevil) inside vm.runInContext (rce/rceOccupy challenges). LLM review assigns CWE-94 (code injection) matching the real RCE class; semgrep only emitted CWE-1104 (unmaintained-component) at this locus.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: user JSON body reaches safeEval in a vm context with a 2s timeout (DoS/escape vector).
findings.recommendation: Remove dynamic eval of user input; parse JSON safely.

findings.title: SSTI / code injection via eval of username token
findings.detail: eval(code) where code is extracted from the user-controlled username via #{...} (usernameXss challenge). Confirmed: `const code = username?.substring(...); username = eval(code)`.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: #{...} body extracted from username and eval'd.
findings.recommendation: Remove eval; render usernames as data, never code.

findings.title: Path traversal / poison null byte in res.sendFile
findings.detail: res.sendFile(path.resolve('ftp/', file)) on user file param after a null-byte cutoff that does not block dot-dot traversal (directoryListing/nullByte challenges). LLM review assigns CWE-22/158 matching the GT taxonomy; semgrep emitted CWE-73 at this locus.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: only null-byte cutoff + slash check; `..%2f..%2f` traverses; `%00` bypasses extension check.
findings.recommendation: Canonicalize and confine resolved path under the intended root; reject traversal sequences.

findings.title: Local file read / path traversal via path.resolve(req.body.layout)
findings.detail: path.resolve(req.body.layout) rendered as a template (lfr challenge); arbitrary file inclusion guarded only by a substring denylist (ftp/ctf.key/encryptionkeys). Tool-missed by semgrep; recovered by LLM review of the render() data flow.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: req.body.layout resolved and rendered; denylist substring check is bypassable for other sensitive files.
findings.recommendation: Restrict layout to an allowlist of known template names.

findings.title: SSRF via fetch(req.body.imageUrl)
findings.detail: fetch(url) where url = req.body.imageUrl with no host/scheme allowlist (ssrf challenge). Confirmed: `const url = req.body.imageUrl; ... const response = await fetch(url)`. Tool-missed by semgrep; recovered by LLM review.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: server fetches an attacker-supplied URL with no SSRF guard; reachable for logged-in users.
findings.recommendation: Validate scheme+host against an allowlist; block internal/metadata addresses.

findings.title: XSS via bypassSecurityTrustHtml on product description
findings.detail: sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml(tableData[i].description) on server-supplied product description (restfulXss challenge), defeating Angular's built-in escaping; rendered via [innerHTML]. Tool-missed by semgrep (no rule emitted for the Angular sanitizer-bypass sink); recovered by LLM source review.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: bypassSecurityTrustHtml on attacker-controllable description bound to [innerHTML] in search-result.component.html.
findings.recommendation: Do not bypass Angular sanitization; render as text or sanitize server-side.

findings.title: DOM XSS via bypassSecurityTrustHtml on search query param
findings.detail: sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml(queryParam) on the user-controlled search query param (localXss/xssBonus challenges), bound to [innerHTML]="searchValue". Tool-missed by semgrep; recovered by LLM source review.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: queryParam from route.snapshot.queryParams.q reaches bypassSecurityTrustHtml then [innerHTML].
findings.recommendation: Do not bypass sanitization on user input; bind as text.

findings.title: Weak password hashing (unsalted MD5)
findings.detail: crypto.createHash('md5') used as the password hash (weakPassword challenge). Confirmed: `export const hash = (data) => crypto.createHash('md5')...`. Tool-missed by semgrep; recovered by LLM review of the crypto primitive.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: unsalted MD5 used for password hashing at lib/insecurity.ts:43.
findings.recommendation: Use bcrypt/scrypt/argon2 with per-user salt.

findings.title: Hardcoded RSA private key used to sign JWTs
findings.detail: The RSA private key used to sign JWTs is embedded as a string literal in source at lib/insecurity.ts:23 (`const privateKey = '-----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----...'`). Tool-missed at this locus by semgrep (it flagged the *use* at line 56); recovered by LLM review identifying the literal declaration.
findings.reproduction: static-confirmed: full PEM RSA private key literal at line 23, used by authorize()/deluxeToken().
findings.recommendation: Load signing key from a secret store / env; rotate the exposed key.

findings.title: XSS via bypassSecurityTrustHtml on feedback comment
findings.detail: feedbacks[i].comment built into an HTML template string then passed to bypassSecurityTrustHtml and bound to [innerHTML]. feedback.comment is user-controlled. Real XSS sink not in the conservative GT.
findings.recommendation: Render feedback as text; do not bypass sanitization.

findings.title: Stored XSS via bypassSecurityTrustHtml on user.email (admin panel)
findings.detail: user.email (from user-list API, attacker-controlled at registration) wrapped in bypassSecurityTrustHtml inside a template string, bound to [innerHTML] in the admin table. Real stored-XSS sink not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Render email as text; do not bypass sanitization.

findings.title: Stored XSS via bypassSecurityTrustHtml on feedback.comment (admin panel)
findings.detail: feedback.comment passed to bypassSecurityTrustHtml, bound to [innerHTML] in admin feedback table. Real stored-XSS sink not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Render comment as text; do not bypass sanitization.

findings.title: XSS via bypassSecurityTrustHtml on lastLoginIp
findings.detail: payload.data.lastLoginIp (from JWT, attacker-influenceable via X-Forwarded-For at login) passed to bypassSecurityTrustHtml then bound to [innerHTML]. Real reflected-XSS class sink not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Render IP as text; validate/escape.

findings.title: XSS via bypassSecurityTrustHtml on orderId
findings.detail: results.data[0].orderId from order-tracking API wrapped in bypassSecurityTrustHtml. Real XSS class sink if orderId stored from attacker input; not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Render orderId as text.

findings.title: innerHTML = snarkdown(hint.text) without sanitization
findings.detail: textBox.innerHTML = snarkdown(hint.text); snarkdown renders markdown to HTML without sanitization. Real XSS class pattern (data currently operator-controlled scenarios). Not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Sanitize snarkdown output before assigning to innerHTML.

findings.title: Hardcoded HMAC key
findings.detail: crypto.createHmac('sha256', 'pa4qacea4VK9t9nGv7yZtwmj') — hardcoded HMAC key literal at line 44. Real CWE-798 at a locus distinct from GT-014.
findings.recommendation: Load HMAC key from secret store.

findings.title: Hardcoded RSA key reused as HMAC secret (deluxeToken)
findings.detail: crypto.createHmac('sha256', privateKey) at line 152 reuses the hardcoded RSA private key literal as an HMAC secret. Real CWE-798 usage, distinct locus from GT-014.
findings.recommendation: Use a dedicated, externally-managed HMAC secret.

findings.title: Path traversal in res.sendFile (encryptionkeys/)
findings.detail: res.sendFile(path.resolve('encryptionkeys/', file)) with only a slash check — dot-dot traversal to arbitrary files. Real path-traversal locus not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Confine resolved path under the intended root.

findings.title: Path traversal in res.sendFile (logs/)
findings.detail: res.sendFile(path.resolve('logs/', file)) with only a slash check — arbitrary file read via traversal (accessLogDisclosure). Not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Confine resolved path under the intended root.

findings.title: Path traversal in res.sendFile (ftp/quarantine/)
findings.detail: res.sendFile(path.resolve('ftp/quarantine/', file)) with only a slash check — same traversal class. Not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Confine resolved path under the intended root.

findings.title: Open redirect at route locus
findings.detail: res.redirect(toUrl) where toUrl = query.to and isRedirectAllowed uses a bypassable substring check (redirectChallenge). Route-level locus distinct from GT-004 (lib/insecurity.ts:138).
findings.recommendation: Validate target host against an exact allowlist.

findings.title: XSS via subtitle injection into script tag
findings.detail: subs injected raw into a <script id="subtitle"> response with no escaping (videoXss challenge). Real XSS sink not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Escape/validate subtitle content; serve as data.

findings.title: Directory listing enabled on /ftp
findings.detail: serveIndex('ftp', { icons: true }) intentionally enables directory listing (directoryListing challenge). Real CWE-548 info exposure, not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Disable directory listing on sensitive mounts.

findings.title: Directory listing enabled on /encryptionkeys
findings.detail: serveIndex('encryptionkeys', ...) exposes key file names. Real CWE-548, not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Disable directory listing on the key directory.

findings.title: bypassSecurityTrustHtml on captcha image data
findings.detail: sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml(data.image) on server-supplied captcha SVG bound to [innerHTML]. SVG can carry script; weak sanitization-bypass pattern. Not in GT.
findings.recommendation: Render captcha as not innerHTML, or sanitize.

findings.title: eval of arithmetic captcha expression
findings.detail: eval(expression) to compute the captcha answer. Expression is server-generated here, but eval on a string is a dangerous primitive (variant of the SSTI class).
findings.recommendation: Replace eval with a safe arithmetic evaluator.

findings.title: bypassSecurityTrustHtml on challenge.description
findings.detail: sanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml(challenge.description) — challenge descriptions are app config, but the sanitizer-bypass pattern is flagged for consistency. Likely low exploitability.
findings.recommendation: Avoid bypassing sanitization; render as text where possible.

limitations.impact: review waves run by the orchestrator inline across source slices, not as N separate processes; methodology (real source-grounded LLM review per slice) preserved, labelled detection=manual
high-severity GT-class findings statically reproduced from source data-flow; no live runtime
